chains.title: rs642961 alters TF binding to promote detrimental IRF6 expression, increasing cleft lip risk (A=Risk).

links.claim: The reference allele (A) binds TF Tbx24 more strongly than the alternative allele (G), leading to altered TF occupancy and expression regulation.
The variant rs642961 is located within the enhancer region ENSR1_B3JM9C, which is marked as an active distal enhancer-like element.
The element ENSR1_B3JM9C regulates IRF6 expression, which is indirectly supported by L2G scoring.
IRF6 plays a known role in craniofacial development, linking this regulation to relevant cell types.
The risk allele (A) alters IRF6 expression in a manner consistent with the observed association between rs642961 and orofacial cleft risk.

predictions: The risk allele (A) influences IRF6 expression leading to increased orofacial cleft risk.
falsified_if: No detectable binding of Tbx24 to the variant location.
The functional relationship is indirect or does not lead to altered IRF6 expression.

chains.title: Null hypothesis: rs642961 is a passenger mutation or linked causal variant with no TF-mediated regulatory effect.
predictions: The regulatory effect of rs642961 on disease risk is independent of transcription factor binding and subsequent changes in gene expression.
falsified_if: A TF is found to bind rs642961 and modulate the expression of IRF6, UTP25, C1orf74, or TRAF3IP3, correlating with the disease risk.

chains.title: rs642961 alters TF binding to promote detrimental UTP25 expression, increasing cleft lip risk (A=Risk).

links.claim: The reference allele (A) of rs642961 binds TF Egr2 more strongly than the alternative allele (G).
The variant lies within the accessible enhancer ENSR1_B3JM9C, facilitating interaction with Egr2.
The element ENSR1_B3JM9C regulates UTP25 expression, evidenced by high L2G scores.
UTP25 is expressed in craniofacial and dental tissues, making this cell type relevant for the phenotype.
Altered UTP25 expression linked to rs642961 contributes to orofacial cleft risk, consistent with the risk allele A.

predictions: The risk allele (A) influences UTP25 expression leading to increased orofacial cleft risk.
falsified_if: No detectable binding of Egr2 to the variant location.
The risk is not mediated by changes in UTP25 expression.

chains.title: rs642961 alters TF binding to promote detrimental TRAF3IP3 expression, increasing cleft lip risk (A=Risk).

links.claim: The reference allele (A) of rs642961 binds TF STAT3 more strongly than the alternative allele (G).
The enhancer ENSR1_B3JM9C mediates the regulatory influence of the rs642961 variant on TRAF3IP3.
The element ENSR1_B3JM9C regulates TRAF3IP3 expression, supported by low-confidence eQTL data.
STAT3 and TRAF3IP3 function are implicated in inflammatory processes relevant to congenital defects.
Altered TRAF3IP3 levels due to the risk allele A contribute to orofacial cleft risk.

predictions: The risk allele (A) influences TRAF3IP3 expression leading to increased orofacial cleft risk.
falsified_if: No detectable binding of STAT3 to the variant location.
The risk is not mediated by changes in TRAF3IP3 expression.

grades_v0.reason: E01 only reports a regulatory_region_variant and an enhancer overlap; it provides no TF binding prediction, no allele-specific binding assay, and never mentions Tbx24. The claim that A binds Tbx24 more strongly than G is unsupported.

E03 supports that rs642961 lies in a dELS with active enhancer marks, but the marks are maxima over biosamples and there is no evidence that this element is regulated by Tbx24 or active in neural crest cells.
E02 places IRF6 9.7 kb away and E05 gives an L2G score of 0.67 for IRF6 in one credible set, but there is no eQTL, chromatin-contact, or perturbation evidence that ENSR1_B3JM9C regulates IRF6.
E06 provides only two PMIDs/titles, neither quoted to show IRF6 function in neural crest cells. No expression or cell-type-specific epigenetic evidence is cited.

E04 does associate rs642961 with orofacial clefts (p=2e-6, effect allele A), but it does not measure IRF6 expression. The step also conflicts with the chain direction: H2 predicts A is protective, while the GWAS effect allele A is the cleft-associated allele.
E01 does not report Egr2 binding or any allele-specific TF binding. No binding prediction or assay supports stronger A-allele Egr2 binding.
E03 supports location within an accessible dELS, but not that this enhancer interacts with Egr2; biosample-specific activity is unavailable.
E05 has the best L2G score for UTP25 (0.75), but this is indirect fine-mapping evidence and there is no UTP25 eQTL, 3D contact, or perturbation showing the element regulates UTP25.
E03 only lists nearby genes and does not establish UTP25 expression in craniofacial or dental/oral epithelial progenitors.

E04 links the variant to orofacial clefts, but does not connect UTP25 expression to cleft risk. The chain prediction says A lowers risk, whereas the GWAS cleft effect allele is A, creating a direction inconsistency.
E01 provides no STAT3 binding evidence or allele-specific binding data. The claim that G binds STAT3 more strongly is unsupported.
E03 places the variant in a dELS, but the specific claim that this enhancer mediates regulation of TRAF3IP3 is not supported by any cited evidence.
E05 includes low-PIP eQTL credible sets for TRAF3IP3 (PIP 0.02-0.04) and an L2G score of 0.53, which is indirect and does not establish that ENSR1_B3JM9C regulates TRAF3IP3.
E05 only provides immune-context eQTL sets for TRAF3IP3; it does not support STAT3 function, inflammatory mechanisms, or relevance to congenital defects.

E04 reports orofacial cleft association with effect allele A, not G. The claim that the G allele is the cleft risk allele is contradicted by the cited cleft GWAS row and is supported only by unrelated blood-pressure signals.

grades_final.reason: E01 is only a VEP regulatory-region annotation and provides no Tbx24 binding, allele-specific occupancy, or QBiC/SELEX evidence for A>G. The TF choice is unsupported.
E03 shows rs642961 lies within EH38E2863563, a dELS with DNase/H3K27ac signal, consistent with the ENSR1_B3JM9C active enhancer claim.
E02 gives only 9.7 kb proximity to IRF6, and E05 L2G prioritizes IRF6 genetically; neither directly shows that ENSR1_B3JM9C regulates IRF6 expression. No IRF6 eQTL or perturbation is cited.
E06 titles mention IRF6/orofacial cleft association but do not show IRF6 function in neural crest cells or establish the claimed cell-type link.
E04 supports an orofacial cleft association with effect allele A, but it does not show altered IRF6 expression, nor does the cited evidence define the direction from A-binding to IRF6 expression.
E01 contains no Egr2 binding or allele-specific data. E08 additionally reports no Egr2 ChIP-seq peak containing the variant, contrary to the claim. QBiC coverage is not checked.
E03 supports an accessible dELS at the variant, but it does not show Egr2 interaction with ENSR1_B3JM9C; the Egr2 part of the claim is unsupported.
E05 provides L2G priority for UTP25, but L2G is genetic gene prioritization, not evidence that ENSR1_B3JM9C regulates UTP25 expression. No UTP25 eQTL or perturbation is cited.
E03 only lists nearby genes; it does not show UTP25 expression in craniofacial or dental tissues or support the specific progenitor cell type.
E04 supports association with orofacial clefts for allele A, but no cited evidence links UTP25 expression to rs642961 or to cleft risk.

E01 provides no STAT3 binding or allele-specific data. Although E09 reports a STAT3 ChIP-seq peak containing the variant in MCF10A, it is not allele-specific and is not cited for this link; it cannot support A>G differential binding.
E03 supports that the variant lies in a dELS, but its nearby genes are IRF6, UTP25, and C1orf74, not TRAF3IP3; no evidence shows ENSR1_B3JM9C mediates TRAF3IP3 regulation.
E05 contains low-confidence TRAF3IP3 eQTL credible sets (PIP 0.02-0.04) and L2G scores, but these are genetic associations, not direct evidence that the enhancer regulates TRAF3IP3 expression.
E05 does not establish STAT3/TRAF3IP3 inflammatory function or relevance to congenital defects in immune cells; the cited evidence is eQTL/L2G context only.
E04 supports an orofacial cleft association with effect allele A, but no cited evidence shows TRAF3IP3 expression changes due to rs642961 or that such changes contribute to cleft risk.

checks.why: The H2 binding link is entirely unsupported; checking whether Tbx24 has an ENCODE ChIP-seq peak containing rs642961 directly tests the claimed binding event.
H3 asserts allele-specific Egr2 binding without any binding evidence; a ChIP peak lookup is the most direct available check.
H4 asserts that the G allele binds STAT3 more strongly, but no STAT3 binding evidence is cited; this check directly tests occupancy at the variant.
